title: An entry machine upload that could not be read is answered as received, so its check-ins can be lost
what: When the door service cannot read a machine's upload of punches (a broken or cut-off send), it quietly treats it as empty, answers the machine that all was received, and still stores the machine's upload marker. The next time the machine calls in it is told the service already holds those punches, so they are never sent again and the members' visits for them are missing. An upload over 2 MB is cut the same way: the rest is dropped and the marker is still stored.
expected: An upload that could not be read in full gets a not-received answer and its marker is not stored, so the machine sends the punches again.
who: owners and members of gyms with an entry machine
how_often: rare: only when an upload breaks or is very large
fix_line: Answer an error and keep the old marker when the upload cannot be read in full

title: Two pieces of branch and entry machine code are never used by the app
what: A rule that puts the current branch first in a list of branches is used nowhere. The plain words for an entry machine's answer to a job (done, refused, not on this model, never answered) are used only by a test: no screen shows the owner whether a job sent to the machine worked.
expected: Unused code is removed, or the machine's answer words are shown on the owner's machine page as intended.
who: developers; owners with entry machines later
fix_line: Delete the unused branch rule and either show or delete the machine answer words

title: The branch receipt example and the demo gym keep their own date rules on the device clock
what: The add-branch card works out the financial year for its sample receipt number with its own rule from the device clock, next to the shared financial-year rule used for real receipts. The demo gym builds its sample times with the device's own time zone, in two copied helpers, while the rest of the app reads times as India time. On a device not set to India time the demo's visit and payment times shift, and near midnight or 1 April the sample can show the wrong day or year.
expected: Both use the app's shared India-time and financial-year rules, kept in one place.
who: owners trying the demo or adding a branch outside India time
how_often: only on a device not set to India time, or at a year change
fix_line: Use the shared financial-year and India-time helpers and drop the copies
